# PR #148 repair correctness review

## A. Verdict

**pass-with-notes** at `03ba18533d267b66d666bfedddb39771535e573d`.

**F001 and F002 closed.** No correctness repair remains in this round. The original AC2/live-attribution and no-op/shim deferrals remain explicit.

## B. Scope

Only `5de084c74c75ea63532bec6f4eb36a9f872092d7..03ba185`: repair `4789a79` and the Linux-only dead-code allowance in `03ba185`. The prior accepted native brake and terminal-retired shutdown stand. Detached checkout stayed clean and pinned; no local builds/tests, mutations, runtime probes or product edits.

## C. F001: exactly-once accounting

Each early return for invalid role, pane-observation failure, out-of-subtree process, vanished pane or identity-observation error now records its outcome before returning. Calls reaching `register_via` are not counted by the route; the service records the settled result once. The shared early tally adds no registry read.

The amended `first_light` regression sends a service refusal and an early invalid-role refusal, then reads ping: total 2, one `shim.paneless.refused`, one `explicit.paneless.refused`, and no made-up name retained. The existing service test retains new/unchanged/refused coverage. This closes the formerly invisible entry-boundary failures without double-counting the service path.

## D. F002: producer labels

Fresh address allocation now defaults to `explicit`; the outer startup loop supplies `lease-retry` after holder standby. The receive loop checks `standingBy` before whether any registration has succeeded. Both producer cases are covered by captured request-body assertions in CI.

Heartbeat selection is unchanged: ordinary lease re-attestation explicitly passes `heartbeat`, while a real holder standby passes `lease-retry`; successful re-attestation clears the standby flag. An already healthy lease does not register. `NativeBridge.register` overwrites the advisory label on the sent copy, so a startup label cannot persistently replace the heartbeat label. Existing lease recovery/stale-answer and terminal-retired cases still pass.

## E. Other repair checks

The per-attempt `Reads` mutex serializes read reservation against closing the tally. A worker attempting its argv read after closure cannot reserve a read and does not call `read_argv_with_ps`; a read reserved before closure is included in the returned tally. The deterministic held-worker test checks an admitted read, closes at count 1, releases the worker and observes refusal with the count unchanged.

Counts retain bounded enum keys and at most 64 short named keys plus overflow; over-64-byte names and unknown claims go to `(other)`, while typed retired/held errors use their recorded seat. Generic refusal counting uses only the existing tally's known-name information, not a new registry query. Overflow, unknown-name and byte-cap regressions pass.

The mutex-based wording is corrected. The final `cfg_attr` changes Linux lint allowance only, not read admission or behavior.

Read-only git head/status/delta and source/test/docs reads; exact-head CI metadata/logs and downloaded JUnit inspection. No build or test was executed locally.
